A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, appendices A–J, and checklists are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification, fine-tuning, label-noise, optimization-dynamics, and timing experiments in Section 5, Figures 1–2, and Appendix J.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds DistilBERT fine-tuning results on GLUE and ASAM versus RW-ASAM experiments.

M1.justification: Appendix J introduces RW-ASAM by applying the proposed reweighting strategy to ASAM, a limited extension to another optimizer. The original RW-SAM objectives, gradient-norm estimator, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v1's empirical coverage concerns image classification. v2 retains this coverage and adds language-model fine-tuning on eight reported GLUE tasks: CoLA, MNLI, MRPC, QNLI, QQP, RTE, SST-2, and STS-B. This substantially extends the evaluated domain and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds AdamW as an evaluated comparator alongside SAM in the GLUE experiment. ASAM, previously cited without reported comparison results, becomes an evaluated comparator to RW-ASAM in Table 9. Existing comparison sets are retained.

E3.justification: The new DistilBERT experiments introduce an AdamW-based fine-tuning protocol with task-dependent batch sizes of 32/64, learning rates of 2e-5/3e-5, and 3/8 epochs, plus linear scheduling, 0.1 warmup, and maximum sequence length 256. Existing vision protocols are unchanged; the newly stated validation-set tuning does not establish that those experiments changed.

E4.justification: Table 9 adds a with/without-reweighting comparison on ASAM across two ResNets and CIFAR-10/100, testing whether the component helps another SAM variant. The existing label-noise, lambda-sensitivity, covariance, and poor-minimum escape analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The new GLUE table reports point scores without uncertainty estimates or run counts, unlike v1's benchmark accuracy tables. Three-run mean/standard-deviation reporting for Tables 1 and 2a is retained, and the new ASAM results use the existing ± format. No increase in runs or new significance-testing procedure is disclosed.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial language-task results: Table 3 reports average scores of 0.809 for RW-SAM, 0.800 for SAM, and 0.804 for AdamW; RW-SAM exceeds SAM on seven tasks and ties on STS-B. Table 9 adds ASAM comparisons with mean accuracy gains of 0.16–0.38 percentage points from reweighting. These are new results, while the earlier vision, analysis, and timing values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The principal SDE framework and approximation orders remain intact. Local revisions include changing Lemma A.3's drift/generator remainder from O(eta rho^(beta+1)) to O(rho^(beta+1)), correcting Appendix C's expected minibatch-gradient norm and normalization denominators, and adding Remark C.1 on epsilon smoothing at zero gradients. Equation 16 becomes approximate, and Appendix G strengthens the claimed squared-estimator bias from O(delta) to O(delta^2).

C1.justification: Both versions claim an SDE explanation of noise-induced m-sharpness, extension from USAM to normalized SAM, and an efficient reweighting algorithm. v2 emphasizes distributed-training motivation and adds supporting experiments without changing these central contributions or their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 4 replaces strict SGN/full-gradient orthogonality with approximate orthogonality or a negligible full gradient near convergence. Remark C.1 newly acknowledges undefined normalization at zero gradients. v2 also softens lambda=0.5 from best across all experiments to consistently strong and discusses further extensions beyond the ASAM experiment.

D1.justification: Table 10 supplies GLUE fine-tuning settings, and Section 5.1 newly specifies that lambda selection used a validation set. These additions improve documentation without establishing changes to existing runs. Hardware disclosure, the original pseudocode, and the checklist's statement that code is not yet available remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands SAM literature coverage across generalization, convergence, optimizer variants, and computational efficiency, including Fisher SAM, Tilted SAM, VASSO, and SAMPA. Additional SGN references are also introduced. The existing theoretical related-work discussion in Appendix F is retained.

P1.justification: v2 revises the abstract and distributed-training introduction, expands related work and experimental prose, standardizes Reweighted SAM/RW-SAM terminology, corrects local wording, and adds acknowledgments. The main section sequence, appendix organization, and most explanatory text remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds GLUE results, ASAM results, and GLUE settings displays as Tables 3, 9, and 10. Existing tables are renumbered and reflowed, and Figures 1–2 move while retaining their curves, axes, and legends. The timing table's WideResNet header is corrected to WideResNet-28-10.

improvement.justification: The GLUE and ASAM experiments broaden support beyond v1's image-only evaluation, added settings improve reproducibility, and Appendix C repairs mathematical inconsistencies. These are useful but limited gains. GLUE lacks metric and uncertainty details, while Appendix G asserts a stronger O(delta^2) bias rate without correspondingly expanding its derivation; these shortcomings limit the overall improvement.
